auth.description: Typeform access token sent as a bearer — a personal access token or an OAuth2 access token
auth.name: typeform.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

config.help: Create one under Account (top-left menu next to your username) → Personal tokens in Typeform, or supply the access token from an OAuth2 app's authorization flow. Typeform shows a newly created personal token once
config.label: Typeform access token
config.name: access_token

description: Typeform: read the authenticated account, forms and their responses, and delete responses

operations.description: Get the Typeform account this access token authenticates as: its account id, display alias, own account email and interface language. Confirms the token resolves. Takes no parameters

alias.description: The account's display alias, shown in Typeform's own UI

email.description: The account owner's own email — never a form respondent's

language.description: The account's interface language, as an IETF language tag, e.g. "en"

operations.description: List the forms in the authenticated account, most recently updated forms sorting available. Returns each form's id, title and public/private status but not its questions — use typeform-form-get for a form's fields

params.description: Forms per page; Typeform defaults this to 10 and caps it at 200
params.name: page_size

id.description: The form's own id — pass this as `form_id` to every other operation below

settings.description: At least `{is_public}`; the vendor's own resource carries more form-level settings this curated connector does not enumerate further

total_items.description: Total forms in the account, which may exceed `items.length` on one page

operations.description: Get one form's own definition: its title, language, rendering type and questions (fields), plus its welcome and thank-you screens. Does not return any response data — use typeform-response-list for that

params.description: The form's own id, from typeform-form-list's `id` field, or the trailing path segment of the form's own URL (the part after `/to/`)
params.name: form_id

fields.description: One entry per question. Each carries at least an id, a ref, a title and a type; some carry nested `properties` and `validations` this curated connector does not enumerate further — read them through rather than assuming a shape

ref.description: The field's own stable reference, distinct from its id — what an answer in a response names this question by

title.description: The question text the form's own author wrote

hidden.description: The variable names of hidden fields this form accepts via URL parameter — the field names only, declared by the form's own author; never a respondent's value

settings.description: Form-level settings (visibility, language, progress bar, meta tags among others); read through rather than assumed — this curated connector does not enumerate every key

type.description: The form's rendering type, e.g. "quiz" or "form"

operations.description: List one form's responses, newest first by default. Paginate with `before`/`after`, each naming the `token` of a response already retrieved, to page toward older or newer responses respectively; `page_size` alone returns only the first page. Each response's `answers` holds whatever that respondent typed or selected — this connector never inspects or filters on answer content

params.description: The form's own id, from typeform-form-list's `id` field, or the trailing path segment of the form's own URL (the part after `/to/`)
params.name: form_id

params.description: Responses per page; Typeform defaults this to 25 and caps it at 1000
params.name: page_size

params.description: Return only responses submitted before this response's own `token` (exclusive) — the cursor for paging toward older responses. Pass the `token` field of the oldest response already retrieved. Omit on the first page
params.name: before

params.description: Return only responses submitted after this response's own `token` (exclusive) — the cursor for paging toward newer responses. Pass the `token` field of the newest response already retrieved. Omit on the first page
params.name: after

params.description: Only include responses at or after this UTC instant, written with no timezone suffix at all, e.g. "2017-07-09T00:00:00" — never a trailing "Z" or a "+HH:MM" offset. Which timestamp this filters (submitted_at, staged_at or landed_at) depends on which response_type is requested
params.name: since

params.description: Only include responses at or before this UTC instant, written with no timezone suffix at all, e.g. "2017-07-09T00:00:00" — never a trailing "Z" or a "+HH:MM" offset. Which timestamp this filters (submitted_at, staged_at or landed_at) depends on which response_type is requested
params.name: until

params.description: Restrict to one or more submission states, comma-separated: started, partial, completed. Omit to receive every state
params.name: response_type

params.description: How to order the returned responses: a fixed field name and a direction, comma-separated
params.name: sort

items.description: This page's responses, in the order `sort` (or the default) puts them

answers.description: One entry per answered question: at minimum `{field: {id, ref, type}, type}` plus exactly one value key named after `type` (text, choice, choices, email, number, boolean, date, url, file_url or payment). The value itself is whatever the respondent typed or selected and is never enumerated or exemplified here

calculated.description: Computed values Typeform's scoring feature attaches

hidden.description: Hidden-field values this response's session was launched with, keyed by the form's own hidden-field variable names (see typeform-form-get's `hidden`). Shape and content depend entirely on the form's own configuration — commonly an email address, a customer id or similar, so this connector never enumerates or exemplifies a value here

landing_id.description: Identifies the browsing session that landed on the form — distinct from the response itself

metadata.description: The submission's own browsing context — browser, platform, referer and network id. Not respondent-authored content

response_id.description: The same value as `token`, under Typeform's other name for it

submitted_at.description: Present once submitted; absent on a still-open partial response

token.description: This response's own opaque id: 32 lowercase hex characters. Pass it as `before` or `after` to page around it

operations.description: Permanently delete one or more of a form's responses by their own token. There is no undelete: once deleted, a response's answers are gone. Deletion is asynchronous — a successful call confirms the request was registered, not that the responses are already gone

params.description: The form's own id, from typeform-form-list's `id` field, or the trailing path segment of the form's own URL (the part after `/to/`)
params.name: form_id

params.description: Comma-separated list of up to 1000 response tokens (the same value as a response's own `token`/`response_id`, from typeform-response-list) to delete permanently
params.name: included_response_ids
